statewide.name: AS-T Track 1 (Chemistry, Geology, Biology, Earth and Environmental Sciences)
general_notes: One statewide agreement covers chemistry and geology: AS-T Track 1 (also biology, environmental/resource sciences and earth science). There is no separate chemistry or geology MRP. Effective Fall 2000, updated Spring 2017 (ICRC Handbook, Oct 2025).

Degree outline (90 quarter credits): 5 English composition; 10 math (two courses at or above intro calculus); 15 humanities and social science; 45-50 pre-major (15 chemistry sequence, 5 third-quarter calculus or approved statistics, 15 biology or physics sequence, 10-15 more physics, geology, organic chemistry, biology or math); 10-15 to reach 90. 2.00 cumulative GPA.
Guarantees: priority admission consideration equal to the DTA, junior standing, and only the extra lower-division general education a DTA holder would need.

Does not guarantee admission to the major. World language and cultural diversity requirements of the university still apply. Pre-major courses count as general education only if on the 'Courses Generally Accepted in Transfer' list.
WSAC links a school list for Track 1 but it was not readable. CWU's April 2024 list accepts Track 1 for junior standing with partial general education.
EvCC builds two Track 1 degrees: Chemistry AS-T (93 credits) and Geology AS-T (90 credits).

statewide.name: AS-T Track 2 (Engineering, Physics, Atmospheric Sciences)
general_notes: Physics majors use AS-T Track 2. Effective Fall 2009, updated Spring 2017; computer science removed in 2025 (ICRC Handbook, Oct 2025).

Degree outline (90 quarter credits): 5 composition; 10 math (two courses at or above intro calculus); 15 humanities and social science; 25 pre-major (15 physics sequence with lab, calculus-based or not; 5 chemistry with lab for engineering or 5 advisor-chosen science for others; 5 third-quarter calculus or approved statistics); 35 more planned with an advisor. 2.00 GPA.
Some universities require calculus-based physics. EvCC's Physics and Astronomy AS-T uses PHYS& 241-243 with labs.

Guarantees: priority admission consideration equal to the DTA, junior standing, only the extra general education a DTA holder would need, and acceptance of approved humanities and social science courses as general education.
Does not guarantee admission to the major. World language and diversity requirements still apply. A university may refuse a general education course that is in the student's major discipline.
Students should check the target major's requirements in the year before transferring.
Mathematics majors are referred to the Math Education MRP, not Track 2.

statewide.name: AS-T Track 1 (Geology and Earth Science)
general_notes: Geology uses the same AS-T Track 1 agreement as chemistry (see wa-statewide-chem). There is no separate geology MRP.
WWU Geology strongly encourages WA community college students to complete Track 1. CWU's Environmental Geological Sciences MAP recommends it.
Track 1 still does not guarantee admission to a geology major (for example, WWU's Phase II prep courses and grades still apply).

statewide.name: Washington Statewide Nursing Transfer Agreements

STEM 101.title: College Success In STEM
STEM 101.description: Orientation to academic and career opportunities in STEM, with guest speakers from industry and universities and development of skills that promote success in college. Satisfies COLL 101 requirement for new degree seeking students.

STEM 102.title: Equity in STEM
STEM 102.description: Project-based introduction to STEM focusing on problem solving, mathematical reasoning, and communication, built around a team environmental justice project. Covers applied developmental math, units and dimensions, precision and tolerance, teamwork, and basic software.

COLL 101.title: College Success
COLL 101.description: College success strategies including college resources and student services, financing college, time management, learning strategies, choosing a major, and preparing an academic plan.

ENGL 98.title: Intro to College Writing
ENGL 98.description: Writing and revising paragraphs and essays, covering the writing process, diction, grammar, essay patterns, and rhetorical devices. Equivalent to TS 98 and HSC 98; credit cannot be earned in both ENGL 98 and either TS 98 or HSC 98.
ENGL 98.prereq_text: Completion of ENGL 97 or equivalent with a grade of C or higher

ENGL& 101.title: English Composition I
ENGL& 101.description: Writing clear, unified, coherent, well-developed essays of increasing complexity with an emphasis on critical thinking, about or springing from literary or nonliterary texts.
ENGL& 101.prereq_text: Completion of ENGL 98 or equivalent with a grade of C or higher.

ENGL& 235.title: Technical Writing and Research
ENGL& 235.description: Writing memoranda, business letters, and technical documents such as definitions, specifications, proposals, instructions, and analytical reports using primary and secondary research and visual design. Emphasizes audience analysis from lay to expert.
ENGL& 235.prereq_text: Completion of ENGL& 101 with a grade of C or higher.

MATH& 141.title: Precalc I: College Algebra
MATH& 141.description: College-level algebra; first of a two-course sequence for students intending to take calculus beginning with MATH& 151. Functions and graphs, polynomial and rational functions, exponential and logarithmic functions, conics, non-linear systems, and determinants.
MATH& 141.prereq_text: MATH 96 or equivalent with a grade of C or higher

MATH& 142.title: Precalculus II: Trig
MATH& 142.description: College-level trigonometry; second course in the two-course sequence leading to MATH& 151. Right-triangle and general-angle trigonometry, identities, inverses, trig equations, polar coordinates, parametric equations, and vectors.
MATH& 142.prereq_text: MATH& 141 or equivalent with a grade of C or higher

MATH& 144.title: Pre-Calc I & II: Review
MATH& 144.description: A refresher course in college algebra and trigonometry for students planning to take the calculus sequence beginning with MATH& 151. Polynomial, rational, exponential, logarithmic, and trigonometric functions, conic sections, and an introduction to vectors.
MATH& 144.prereq_text: One year of high school precalculus or college equivalent; or permission of a math instructor
MATH& 144.placement: One year of high school precalculus or college equivalent; or permission of a math instructor

MATH& 151.title: Calculus I
MATH& 151.description: First course in the calculus sequence: limits, continuity, differentiation and antidifferentiation of algebraic and transcendental functions with applications. For engineering, science, and math majors.
MATH& 151.prereq_text: MATH& 142 or 144 or equivalent with a grade of C or higher

MATH& 152.title: Calculus II
MATH& 152.description: Second course in the calculus sequence: integration and applications of definite integrals (areas, volumes, work, hydrostatic force, centers of mass), polar and parametric calculus, numerical techniques, and improper integrals.
MATH& 152.prereq_text: MATH& 151 with a grade of C or higher

MATH& 163.title: Calculus 3
MATH& 163.description: Third course in the calculus sequence: infinite series, power series and Taylor polynomials, vectors in 2D and 3D, lines and planes, partial differentiation, and double integrals in rectangular and polar coordinates.
MATH& 163.prereq_text: MATH& 152 with a grade of C or higher

MATH& 264.title: Calculus 4
MATH& 264.description: Fourth course in the calculus sequence: triple integrals, vector-valued functions and space curves, directional derivatives and gradients, line and surface integrals, and the theorems of Green, Stokes, and Divergence.
MATH& 264.prereq_text: MATH& 163 with a grade of C or higher

MATH 260.title: Linear Algebra
MATH 260.description: Theory and applications of matrices, linear systems, determinants, Euclidean vector spaces and subspaces, linear transformations and change of bases, and eigenvalues and eigenvectors.
MATH 260.prereq_text: Completion of MATH&163 with a C or higher

MATH 261.title: Differential Equations
MATH 261.description: Introductory ordinary differential equations: existence and uniqueness, first-order linear and non-linear methods, higher-order linear equations, series solutions, systems of equations, and Laplace transforms, with applications.
MATH 261.prereq_text: Completion of MATH&163 or MATH& 264 with a C or higher

CHEM& 140.title: General Chem Prep W/Lab
CHEM& 140.description: Measurements, properties and structure of matter, nomenclature, and weight relations, for students needing chemistry background for the CHEM& 161-163 series. Not intended for students with recent high school chemistry, and does not meet nursing program prerequisites.
CHEM& 140.prereq_text: Eligibility for ENGL& 101 AND eligibility for MATH 96
CHEM& 140.placement: Eligibility for ENGL& 101 AND eligibility for MATH 96

CHEM& 161.title: General Chemistry I with Lab
CHEM& 161.description: Properties of matter, atomic theory and structure, periodicity, bonding models, nomenclature, molecular shapes, intermolecular forces, reactions, and stoichiometry. For pre-health professions and all engineering and science majors.
CHEM& 161.prereq_text: Eligibility for ENGL& 101 AND eligibility for MATH& 141. One of the following: CHEM& 140 with a grade of C or higher, or one year of high school chemistry with a C or higher within the last one year, or MATH& 152 with a B+ or higher
CHEM& 161.placement: Eligibility for ENGL& 101 AND eligibility for MATH& 141; alternative to CHEM& 140/MATH& 152: one year of high school chemistry with a C or higher within the last one year

CHEM& 162.title: General Chemistry II with Lab
CHEM& 162.description: Aqueous reactions (precipitation, acid-base, redox), stoichiometry, thermochemistry, thermodynamics, ideal gases, and properties of liquids, solids, and solutions. For pre-health professions and all engineering and science majors.
CHEM& 162.prereq_text: CHEM& 161 with a grade of C or higher

CHEM& 163.title: General Chemistry III with Lab
CHEM& 163.description: Equilibrium, acid/base and solubility equilibria, buffers, electrochemistry, kinetics, and nuclear chemistry. For pre-health professions and all engineering and science majors.
CHEM& 163.prereq_text: CHEM& 162 with a grade of C or higher.

CHEM& 261.title: Organic Chem W/Lab I
CHEM& 261.description: Chemistry of carbon compounds, with emphasis on structure, nomenclature, reactions, mechanisms, and synthesis of main types of organic compounds.
CHEM& 261.prereq_text: Eligibility for ENGL& 101 and CHEM& 163 with grade of C or higher, or CHEM& 162 with instructor permission.
CHEM& 261.placement: Eligibility for ENGL& 101; or CHEM& 162 with instructor permission (in place of CHEM& 163)

CHEM& 262.title: Organic Chemistry II with Lab
CHEM& 262.description: Continuation of CHEM& 261: structure, nomenclature, reactions, mechanisms, and synthesis of main types of organic compounds.
CHEM& 262.prereq_text: CHEM& 261 with grade of C or higher.

CHEM& 263.title: Organic Chemistry III with Lab
CHEM& 263.description: Continuation of CHEM& 262: structure, nomenclature, reactions, mechanisms, and synthesis of main types of organic compounds.
CHEM& 263.prereq_text: CHEM& 262 with grade of C or higher.

BIOL& 221.title: Majors Ecology/Evolution
BIOL& 221.description: Mendelian genetics, evolution, biodiversity of life forms, and ecology. First course of the three-quarter majors series for students intending to major in the sciences.
BIOL& 221.prereq_text: CHEM& 161 (or concurrent enrollment) or equivalent, with a grade of C (2.0) or higher. All prerequisites must be taken within the last five years, OR instructor permission.
BIOL& 221.placement: or equivalent; prerequisites must be taken within the last five years, OR instructor permission

BIOL& 222.title: Majors Cell/Molecular
BIOL& 222.description: Metabolism and energetics, structure and function of biomolecules and cells, and applications of biotechnology and molecular biology. Second course of the three-quarter majors series.
BIOL& 222.prereq_text: BIOL& 221 with a grade of C (2.0) or higher and CHEM& 162 (or concurrent enrollment) with a grade of C (2.0) or higher. All prerequisites must be taken within the last five years, or instructor permission.
BIOL& 222.placement: prerequisites must be taken within the last five years, or instructor permission

BIOL& 223.title: Majors Organismal Physiology
BIOL& 223.description: Animal and plant development and physiology, including photosynthesis. Final course of the three-quarter majors series for students intending to major in the sciences.
BIOL& 223.prereq_text: BIOL& 222 with a grade of C (2.0) or higher and CHEM& 163 (or concurrent enrollment) with a grade of C or higher.

PHYS& 114.title: General Physics I
PHYS& 114.description: First course in the one-year algebra-based General Physics sequence (PHYS& 114-116), covering motion, force, momentum, and energy.
PHYS& 114.prereq_text: Eligibility for ENGL& 101, AND completion of (or concurrent enrollment in) MATH& 142 or MATH& 144 or equivalent.
PHYS& 114.placement: Eligibility for ENGL& 101; MATH& 142/144 or equivalent

PHYS& 241.title: Engineering Physics I + Lab (PHYS& 231)
PHYS& 241.description: Mechanics. First quarter of the one-year calculus-based sequence (PHYS& 241-243) for engineering and most science majors planning to transfer.
PHYS& 241.prereq_text: MATH& 151 AND PHYS& 114, each with a C or higher, OR passing Physics Placement test, AND eligibility for ENGL& 101.
PHYS& 241.placement: OR passing Physics Placement test (catalog wording is ambiguous whether the test replaces both MATH& 151 and PHYS& 114 or only PHYS& 114); AND eligibility for ENGL& 101

PHYS& 231.title: Engineering Physics I Lab
PHYS& 231.description: Analysis techniques for modeling experimental results and uncertainties, teamwork, scientific and engineering report writing, and independent research skills. Offered concurrently with PHYS& 241, though material does not directly parallel it.

PHYS& 242.title: Engineering Physics II + Lab (PHYS& 232)
PHYS& 242.description: Thermodynamics and waves. Second quarter of the one-year calculus-based sequence (PHYS& 241-243) for engineering and most science majors planning to transfer.
PHYS& 242.prereq_text: PHYS& 241 AND MATH& 152, each with a C or higher.

PHYS& 232.title: Engineering Physics II Lab
PHYS& 232.description: Analysis techniques for modeling experimental results and uncertainties, teamwork, scientific and engineering report writing, and independent research skills. Offered concurrently with PHYS& 242, though material does not directly parallel it.

PHYS& 243.title: Engineering Physics III + Lab (PHYS& 233)
PHYS& 243.description: Electromagnetism. Third quarter of the one-year calculus-based sequence (PHYS& 241-243) for engineering and most science majors planning to transfer.
PHYS& 243.prereq_text: PHYS& 242 AND MATH& 163, each with a C or higher.  Lab PHYS& 233: Completion of MFG T 103 or PHYS 130 with a C or higher.

PHYS& 233.title: Engineering Physics III Lab
PHYS& 233.description: Development and completion of team-designed experiments on instructor-approved topics, producing a publication-quality report. Offered concurrently with PHYS& 243.
PHYS& 233.prereq_text: Completion of MFG T 103 or PHYS 130 with a C or higher.

MFG T 103.title: Machining Lab for Engineers
MFG T 103.description: Introduces machining and manufacturing processes: setup and operation of manual mills, lathes, drill presses, band saws and other shop tools, basic blueprint reading, and an introduction to 3-axis CNC vertical mills.

ENGR 111.title: Intro Engr I: Model/Analysis
ENGR 111.description: Project-based introduction to engineering analysis, problem solving, and mathematical modeling through team hands-on projects. Topics include engineering for sustainability, teamwork, applying math/physics/chemistry, unit systems, and spreadsheets.
ENGR 111.prereq_text: Eligibility for ENGL& 101 AND eligibility for MATH 96.
ENGR 111.placement: Eligibility for ENGL& 101 AND eligibility for MATH 96

ENGR& 114.title: Engineering Graphics
ENGR& 114.description: Methods of depicting three-dimensional objects and communicating design information, emphasizing parametric solid modeling software. Freehand sketching develops visualization and design communication skills.
ENGR& 114.prereq_text: Eligibility for MATH& 107 or higher; OR completion of ENG T 100
ENGR& 114.placement: Eligibility for MATH& 107 or higher (alternative to ENG T 100)

ENGR 121.title: Intro to Engineering 2: Design
ENGR 121.description: Second course in the Introduction to Engineering sequence, exploring creativity, teamwork, and communication in innovative design. Includes an introduction to computing, microcontroller programming, and basic parameter optimization through hands-on design projects.
ENGR 121.prereq_text: Completion of MATH& 142 and ENGR 111, OR MATH& 142 and STEM 102, OR MATH& 152, all with a C or higher.

CS& 131.title: Computer Science I C++
CS& 131.description: Software development in C++ covering data types, variables, control structures, modular design, pointers, dynamic memory, and arrays, with an introduction to memory management and object-oriented programming.
CS& 131.prereq_text: Completion of CS 110 or ENGR 121 with a C or higher

CS& 141.title: Computer Science I Java
CS& 141.description: Basic programming concepts for engineering and science problems in Java: classes, objects, methods, variables and types, control structures, arrays, strings, and collections and iterators.
CS& 141.prereq_text: Completion of CS 110 or ENGR 121 with a C or higher.

BUS& 101.title: Intro to Business
BUS& 101.description: An introduction to the American business system in a global, Internet-influenced economy, covering ethics and social responsibility, management, finance, human resources, entrepreneurship, and marketing.

MATH 86.title: Essential Intermediate Algebra
MATH 86.description: Introductory course in mathematical reasoning, focusing on real-world applications and conceptual understanding.
MATH 86.prereq_text: MATH 76 or equivalent with a grade of C or higher

MATH 96.title: Intermediate Algebra for Precalculus
MATH 96.description: Intermediate algebra for students headed into science, business or engineering: functions, linear systems, polynomials, rational expressions, exponents and radicals, quadratics and exponential functions.
MATH 96.prereq_text: MATH 86 or equivalent with a grade of C or higher

CS 110.title: Intro to Computer Science
CS 110.description: Entry-level introduction to programming fundamentals and basic software design for students new to coding.
CS 110.prereq_text: Eligibility for ENGL& 101 and Eligibility for MATH& 107 or higher.
CS 110.placement: Eligibility for ENGL& 101 and eligibility for MATH& 107 or higher

ENGL& 102.title: Composition II
ENGL& 102.description: Researching and writing multi-source essays: audience, purpose, style, writing process, and source evaluation, documentation, and synthesis.
ENGL& 102.prereq_text: Completion of ENGL& 101 with a C or better

MATH& 107.title: Math In Society
MATH& 107.description: College-level applications of mathematics to management, social sciences, biology and other fields: discrete math, graph theory, probability and statistics. For students not pursuing calculus or the sciences.
MATH& 107.prereq_text: Completion of MATH 86 or equivalent with a C or higher OR concurrent enrollment in MATH 102.

any.note: concurrent enrollment in a paired MATH 102 section

MATH& 146.title: Intro to Statistics
MATH& 146.description: Introductory statistics for any major: descriptive methods, probability, sampling distributions, hypothesis testing, confidence intervals, and correlation.
MATH& 146.prereq_text: MATH 86 or equivalent with a grade of C or higher

MATH 102.title: Algebra for Math in Society
MATH 102.description: Just-in-time algebra review for MATH& 107: real numbers, exponents, scientific notation, linear equations and inequalities, ratios, proportions, and percentages. Only for students in a paired MATH& 107 section.

TS 86.title: Intermediate Algebra
TS 86.description: Transitional Studies course in mathematical reasoning with real-world applications: ratios and percentages, linear models, quadratic applications, algebraic manipulation, measures of center, and geometry. Equivalent to MATH 86 (credit cannot be earned in both).
TS 86.prereq_text: Eligibility for HSC, TS, or MATH 86.Students must have completed the TS orientation & assessment or taken a TS class within the last 6 months. Contact Transitional Studies at transitional@everettcc.edu or Rainier Hall Rm 227.
TS 86.placement: Eligibility for HSC, TS, or MATH 86; TS orientation & assessment, or a TS class within the last 6 months

TS 98.title: Intro/College Essays
TS 98.description: Transitional Studies preparation for college writing: formal academic writing and essay structure, with an introduction to information literacy, research, and documentation styles.
TS 98.prereq_text: Students must have completed the Transitional Studies orientation and assessment or taken a TS class within the last 6 months. Please contact Transitional Studies at transitional@everettcc.edu or Rainier Hall Rm 227.
TS 98.placement: Transitional Studies orientation and assessment, or a TS class within the last 6 months

PHIL& 120.title: Symbolic Logic
PHIL& 120.description: Methods for distinguishing sound from unsound reasoning: categorical, propositional, and predicate logic, with hands-on problems and proofs.

BUS 110.title: Business Communications
BUS 110.description: Business communication in global workplaces: good/neutral/bad-news messages, persuasive requests, short reports, presentations, listening, and nonverbal communication across cultures.

BUS 165.title: Found of Leadership & Service
BUS 165.description: Employment documents, customer service fundamentals, and leadership and management skills, emphasizing a service culture and a loyal workforce.

CMST& 210.title: Interpersonal Communication
CMST& 210.description: Theories and skills for communication in social, family, and work settings: self-concept, perception, language, nonverbal cues, relationships, and conflict.

CMST& 230.title: Small Group Communication
CMST& 230.description: How people interact in social, family, learning, and problem-solving groups: participation, power, leadership, and conflict management.

CL 101.title: Intro to Computer Applications
CL 101.description: How computers work: device types, input and storage, operating systems, search engines, the Windows environment, application programs, and file management. BT 100 or keyboarding speed of 20 wpm recommended.

BIOL& 100.title: Survey of Biology
BIOL& 100.description: Introductory overview of living organisms, scientific methods, and biology's relevance to people and society; for non-science majors.
BIOL& 100.prereq_text: Eligibility for ENGL& 101 and eligibility for MATH 96
BIOL& 100.placement: Eligibility for ENGL& 101 and eligibility for MATH 96

CHEM& 121.title: Introduction to Chemistry
CHEM& 121.description: Introductory survey of chemistry (structure, bonding, reactions, gases, equilibrium) for liberal arts, nursing, and allied health students.
CHEM& 121.prereq_text: Eligibility for ENGL& 101 and eligibility for MATH 96
CHEM& 121.placement: Eligibility for ENGL& 101 and eligibility for MATH 96

GEOL 102.title: Intro to Geological Science I
GEOL 102.description: Earth's composition, structure, and dynamic processes: earthquakes, volcanoes, plate tectonics, and mountain building (lab).
GEOL 102.prereq_text: Eligibility for ENGL& 101 AND eligibility for MATH 86.
GEOL 102.placement: Eligibility for ENGL& 101 AND eligibility for MATH 86

NUTR& 101.title: Nutrition
NUTR& 101.description: Nutrition across life stages: healthy eating guidelines, nutrient functions and sources, metabolism, energy balance, sports nutrition, and disease prevention.
NUTR& 101.prereq_text: Eligibility for ENGL& 101 AND eligibility for MATH 96.
NUTR& 101.placement: Eligibility for ENGL& 101 AND eligibility for MATH 96

BIOL& 232.title: Human Physiology
BIOL& 232.description: How the major organ systems function and work together: nervous, muscular, endocrine, cardiovascular, renal, reproductive, immune and respiratory systems. Lecture and lab.
BIOL& 232.prereq_text: BIOL& 211 and BIOL& 231, or BIOL& 221, BIOL& 222 and BIOL& 223; and CHEM& 121, or CHEM& 161 and CHEM& 162; each with a grade of C or higher, taken within the last five years or instructor permission

MFG T 100.title: Success & Safety
MFG T 100.description: Covers industrial and manufacturing trade standards, workflows, and operating procedures, along with workplace soft skills and the reasoning and communication habits employers expect. Connects these expectations to advanced manufacturing fields such as composites, engineering technology, precision machining, and mechatronics/robotics.

MFG T 101.title: Introduction to Machining
MFG T 101.description: Introduction to machining and manufacturing processes commonly used in the industry. The course covers setup and operations of manual mills, lathes, drill presses, band saws, and basic blueprint reading.
MFG T 101.prereq_text: MFG T 100 with a grade of C or higher, or concurrent enrollment in MFG T 100, or instructor permission

MFG T 104.title: Machine Operator 1
MFG T 104.description: Covers applied machinist math, measurement, basic blueprint reading, and operation of conventional lathes, mills, and small shop tools, with an introduction to CNC machines. It also teaches manufacturing processes, shop safety, and teamwork.

MFG T 105.title: Machine Operator 2
MFG T 105.description: Covers advanced blueprint interpretation, including GD&T, along with geometry and trigonometry applications, while deepening CNC programming and operation skills. Students may repeat the course twice for credit.
MFG T 105.prereq_text: Completion of MFG 104 with a grade of C or higher.

MFG T 107.title: Machining with Mastercam
MFG T 107.description: Introduction to the Computer Aided Manufacturing software Mastercam.
MFG T 107.prereq_text: MFG T 105 with a grade of C or higher

MFG T 108.title: NC Programming with Vericut
MFG T 108.description: Introduction to the Computer Aided Manufacturing software Vericut. Students learn to use this software, which simulates CNC machining.
MFG T 108.prereq_text: MFG T 101 or MFG T 113, with a grade of C or higher, or instructor permission

MFG T 109.title: NC Programming with CATIA
MFG T 109.description: Introduction to the Computer Aided Manufacturing software CATIA. Students will be able to use the software used for creating and simulating CNC machining.
MFG T 109.prereq_text: MFG T 101 and ENG T 185, each with a grade of C or higher

MFG T 113.title: CNC Cutting Solutions
MFG T 113.description: Covers waterjet cutting, three-axis routing, and fabric cutting machines. Students create CAD/CAM programs for each machine, then practice setup, operation, troubleshooting, corrective actions, and part inspection to meet industry standards.
MFG T 113.prereq_text: MFG T 100 with a grade of C or higher, or concurrent enrollment in MFG T 100

MFG T 117.title: Blueprint Reading & Schematics
MFG T 117.description: Drafting fundamentals and orthographic interpretation necessary to read, manipulate and understand a mechanical part print.

MFG T 229.title: Manufacturing Team Project
MFG T 229.description: A capstone course where students apply what they've learned about manufacturing technology in a team project, designing and producing a manufactured good and writing a final report.

MFG T 230.title: Mfg Team Project Aerospace
MFG T 230.description: Students collaborate with peers from multiple schools in distributed teams through the AerosPACE program to design, build, and fly a 3/4 scale aircraft. The work covers concept development, design documentation, prototype fabrication, testing, analysis, and reporting.

ENG T 100.title: Engineering Graphics
ENG T 100.description: Introductory course in 2D computer-aided design software for creating, modifying, analyzing, and optimizing designs. Students apply drafting standards, such as borders, orthographic views, and auxiliary views, to produce engineering drawings.
ENG T 100.prereq_text: DEVED 96 or CL 101 with a grade of C or higher, or instructor permission

ENG T 101.title: Technical Problem Solving
ENG T 101.description: Solving problems involving manufactured assemblies for students in manufacturing technology. Covers engineering and mechanical scales and precision measuring instruments, and applies basic algebra, geometry, and trigonometry to problems such as volumes and weights.

ENG T 103.title: Introduction to Revit
ENG T 103.description: Introduces the architectural design and documentation tools in Revit, including the Building Information Modeling interface and the fundamentals of creating a building model.
ENG T 103.prereq_text: Completion of ENG T 100 with a C or higher

ENG T 108.title: Engineering Graphics: 3D CAD
ENG T 108.description: Fundamentals of design with introduction to a 3D parametric CAD modeler in the preparation of designs and working drawings.
ENG T 108.prereq_text: Completion of DEVED 96 or CL 101 with a C or higher, or instructor permission

ENG T 111.title: Intro Engineering Tech Design
ENG T 111.description: Introduces CAD software as a tool for engineering technical design, covering blueprint drafting and programming 3D printers to produce additive mechanical and structural parts.
ENG T 111.prereq_text: Prerequisite may be waived by instructor permission.

ENG T 185.title: Intro to Catia 3DE
ENG T 185.description: Introduces parametric, three-dimensional modeling in CATIA 3D Experience. Students learn to navigate the software, build solid parts using industry best practices, and then assemble and manipulate those parts.
ENG T 185.prereq_text: DEVED 96 or CL 101 with a grade of C or higher

ENG T 193.title: Intermediate CAD W/ Catia 3DE
ENG T 193.description: Techniques for using CATIA 3D Experience to produce working-level engineering drawings: detail and assembly drawings with views, text, dimensions, tolerances, bills of material, borders, and title blocks.
ENG T 193.prereq_text: Completion of ENG T 185 with a C or higher.

ENG T 194.title: Tool Design and Product
ENG T 194.description: Students design tooling fixtures used to make or assemble engineering parts, modeling each one in accurate 3D coordinates with proper product-structure practices, working in collaborative teams.
ENG T 194.prereq_text: Completion of ENG T 185 with a C or higher.

ENG T 195.title: Adv Surfacing with Catia 3DE
ENG T 195.description: Tools and methods from the Generative Structural Analysis, Free Style, Wireframe, and Generative Shape Design workbenches in CATIA 3D Experience.
ENG T 195.prereq_text: Completion of ENG T 193 with a C or higher.

ENG T 196.title: Adv Workbenches with Catia 3DE
ENG T 196.description: Advanced CATIA 3D Experience workbenches: Knowledgeware, DMU Kinematics, Generative Structural Analysis, Generative Sheet Metal Design, Weld Design, and Prismatic Machining.
ENG T 196.prereq_text: Completion of ENG T 193 with a C or higher

ENG T 203.title: AutoCAD II - Intermediate
ENG T 203.description: Intermediate AutoCAD skills for producing engineering drawings more efficiently: layouts and paper space, layer management, reusable blocks, symbols, external references, and attributes for bills of materials.
ENG T 203.prereq_text: Completion of ENG T 100 with a C or higher

ENG T 204.title: Drafting Using CAD
ENG T 204.description: Core drafting skills for mechanical and structural work, including detailing parts, assemblies, and installation drawings in a 3D coordinate system, drawing checking, revisions under ASME and ANSI standards, and bills of materials.
ENG T 204.prereq_text: Completion of ENG T 185 and ENG T 108 with a C or higher.

ENG T 205.title: Precision, Fits, w/ GD&T
ENG T 205.description: Dimensioning and tolerancing theory and application using CAD software, with emphasis on standard tolerances, precision fits, and Geometric Dimensioning and Tolerancing (GD&T), including GD&T through Model Based Definition (MBD).
ENG T 205.prereq_text: Completion of ENG T 204 with a C or higher.

ENG T 217.title: CAD Design Project
ENG T 217.description: CAD design projects for advanced manufacturing and technical design students: take apart a precision mechanical assembly, redesign it, and document the changes in a parametric 3D modeler, including a detailed parts list.
ENG T 217.prereq_text: ENG T 259 and ENG T 193 (or concurrent enrollment), each with a grade C or higher

ENG T 230.title: Mfg Materials and Processes
ENG T 230.description: Survey of materials used in manufacturing and the methods for shaping them into finished parts, how material properties influence selection, and how materials and processes affect feasibility and cost.
ENG T 230.prereq_text: Eligibility for MATH 86 or equivalent OR completion of ENG T 101 with a C or higher.
ENG T 230.placement: Eligibility for MATH 86, or ENG T 101 with a C or higher

ENG T 259.title: Engr Graphics: 3D CAD-CAM
ENG T 259.description: Using a 3D parametric CAD program to produce flat patterns, weldments, machining drawings, bills of material, and title blocks, and 3D CAM software to run a three-axis benchtop milling machine.
ENG T 259.prereq_text: Completion of ENG T 108, or ENGR& 114 or equivalent, with a C or higher.

CT 101.title: Intro to Composites
CT 101.description: Composite materials and how industries use them, with an emphasis on building basic fabrication skills and handling materials safely.

CT 102.title: Composite Technology 1
CT 102.description: Composite manufacturing fundamentals, including resin types, polymer curing, laminate and sandwich-core design, layup methods, and open and closed molding such as wet layup, filament winding, vacuum bagging, VARTM, and LRTM.
CT 102.prereq_text: Eligibility for MATH 76 or equivalent, OR instructor permission.
CT 102.placement: Eligibility for MATH 76, or instructor permission

CT 145.title: Composite Special Projects
CT 145.description: Applying the full composite production process, including reading prints, planning and layout, controlling distortion, and designing fixtures, to design and manufacture an original product independently and in a team.
CT 145.prereq_text: Completion of CT 101 or CT 102 with a C or higher

CT 203.title: Composite Technology 2
CT 203.description: Theory and hands-on application of advanced composite manufacturing methods, plus inspecting and repairing composite damage.
CT 203.prereq_text: Completion of CT 102 with a C or higher.

MECH 118.title: Predictive Maintenance
MECH 118.description: Forecasting-based and scheduled maintenance methods and instruments for factory machinery, plus continuous improvement principles for plant operations, troubleshooting, and repair.
MECH 118.prereq_text: MFG T 100 with a grade of C or higher, or concurrent enrollment in MFG T 100

MECH 119.title: Introduction to Robotics
MECH 119.description: Basics of operating robots, simple programming, interfacing, and material handling within complex mechatronic systems, using interactive robotic devices.
MECH 119.prereq_text: Eligibility for ENGL& 101 AND either ENG T 101 with a grade of C or higher, or eligibility for MATH 86
MECH 119.placement: Eligibility for ENGL& 101, and ENG T 101 (C or higher) or eligibility for MATH 86

MECH 120.title: Electrical Components
MECH 120.description: Functions and physical traits of electrical components and how they fit into complex mechatronics systems, plus schematics, timing diagrams, system specifications, and safety.
MECH 120.prereq_text: Eligibility for ENGL& 101 AND either ENG T 101 with a grade of C or higher, or eligibility for MATH 86
MECH 120.placement: Eligibility for ENGL& 101, and ENG T 101 (C or higher) or eligibility for MATH 86

MECH 121.title: Mechanical Components
MECH 121.description: Basics of mechanical components and electrical drives in a complex mechatronics system. Students will understand the flow of energy, troubleshooting, preventive maintenance and safety issues.
MECH 121.prereq_text: Eligibility for ENGL& 101 AND either ENG T 101 with a grade of C or higher, or eligibility for MATH 86
MECH 121.placement: Eligibility for ENGL& 101, and ENG T 101 (C or higher) or eligibility for MATH 86

MECH 122.title: Elec-Pneumatic Ctrl Circuits
MECH 122.description: Pneumatic, electro-pneumatic, and hydraulic control circuits within complex mechatronics systems: how control elements work and the roles of components in pneumatic and hydraulic setups.
MECH 122.prereq_text: Eligibility for ENGL& 101 AND either ENG T 101 with a grade of C or higher, or eligibility for MATH 86
MECH 122.placement: Eligibility for ENGL& 101, and ENG T 101 (C or higher) or eligibility for MATH 86

MECH 123.title: Digital Fundamentals
MECH 123.description: Core digital logic concepts and an introduction to programmable logic controllers (PLCs) in a mechatronics system. Students write and test small PLC programs on a real system.
MECH 123.prereq_text: MECH 120 with a grade of C or higher

MECH 124.title: Controls and Instrumentation
MECH 124.description: Controls and instrumentation in mechatronic systems: circuit boards, sensors, calibration, loop tuning, and AC, DC, and servo motors, drives, relays, and starters, with practice diagnosing motor and drive faults.
MECH 124.prereq_text: Completion of MECH 123 with a C or higher, OR instructor permission.

MECH 219.title: Industrial Robotics
MECH 219.description: Prepares students for the NOCTI Robotics Certification exam: robot operation, frame setup, basic motion programs, offsets, backups, simulations, six-axis mastering, pick-and-place programming, and 2D vision.
MECH 219.prereq_text: MECH 119 with a grade of C or higher

MECH 295.title: Mechatronics Internship 1
MECH 295.description: Internship developing the basic mechatronics skills needed to work in manufacturing, through instruction-based hands-on learning or on-the-job practice.

MECH 296.title: Mechatronics Internship 2
MECH 296.description: Internship building core mechatronics skills for a manufacturing company, through hands-on work or job-shadowing of manufacturing support functions.

WELD 101.title: Introduction to Welding
WELD 101.description: Introduces welding: shop safety, setup and operation of common fabrication tools and equipment, key metallurgical terms, and the alloying elements used in carbon steel and their effects.
WELD 101.prereq_text: Completion of MFG T 100 with a C or higher, or concurrent enrollment.

WELD 105.title: Intro to Fabrication Planning
WELD 105.description: The planning work that comes before fabrication: material lists, stock inventory, efficient layout, measuring fabrication dimensions, and calculating lengths and weights for weldments in English and metric units.

WELD 106.title: Intro Fabrication Document
WELD 106.description: The documentation used in the welding industry for safety, quality control, production, performance, and daily business operations, and the strengths, limits, and uses of each.

WELD 111.title: Basic Layout
WELD 111.description: Baseline, radial, cylindrical, and triangulation layout methods for flat patterns, pipe intersections, and cones, plus basic lofting as used in sheet metal fabrication and HVAC work.

WELD 150.title: Blueprint Reading for Industry
WELD 150.description: Engineering drawings, lines, and symbols as used in the machine and fabrication trades: blueprint lines, three-view, isometric, and orthographic drawings, and welding symbols.

WELD 151.title: Carbon Steel Metallurgy
WELD 151.description: Metallurgical terminology for carbon steels: metal properties, phase changes, melting and solidification rates, weld bead metallurgy, and heat-affected zones.

WELD 152.title: Weld Base Mtrls and Processes
WELD 152.description: How base metals are classified and identified under SAE, ASTM, and AWS systems, common welding processes and power sources, and reading and writing welding procedures.

WELD 153.title: Non-ferrous Metallurgy
WELD 153.description: Basic metallurgy of stainless steels, aluminum, and cast iron, their heat treatment, material and filler metal designations, and common welding procedures.

WELD 160.title: Intro Weld Nondestructive Test
WELD 160.description: Introduction to nondestructive examination methods, with practice interpreting results and the advantages, limits, and uses of each technique.

WELD 191.title: Basic Arc Welding
WELD 191.description: Manual Shielded Metal Arc Welding with E 6010 and/or E 6011 electrodes, producing fillet and open root welds to industry standards in all positions. May be repeated twice for credit.

WELD 193.title: Basic Pipe Welding
WELD 193.description: Pipe welding with shielded metal arc or gas tungsten arc processes: joint preparation and filler metal selection for the 2G, 5G, and 6G positions, building toward the AWS D1.1 standard.

WELD 194.title: Gas Tungsten Arc Welding
WELD 194.description: Fundamentals and techniques of Gas Tungsten Arc Welding, including setting up and adjusting GTAW equipment for steel, stainless steel, and aluminum.

WELD 195.title: Gas Metal Arc Welding
WELD 195.description: Gas Metal Arc Welding on steel and aluminum, setting up and adjusting GMAW equipment for short arc, spray, and pulse spray transfer.

WELD 211.title: Sheet Metal Fabrication
WELD 211.description: Basic sheet metal fabrication: projects from prints using flat pattern layout, bending sequences, spot welding, hand tools, brakes, roll forms, and punching and notching equipment.

WELD 214.title: Pressbrake/Sub Arc Weld
WELD 214.description: Safety, setup, and operation of sub arc welding on plate and pipe sections and the 120-ton hydraulic press brake, including bending sequences, bump rolling, and basic maintenance.
WELD 214.prereq_text: WELD 195 or WELD 196, AND WELD 210, each with a grade of C or higher

WELD 216.title: Advanced TIG Welding
WELD 216.description: Advanced TIG welding for specialized manufacturing such as aerospace and nuclear, including water-cooled torches, purge systems, and gas lenses.

WELD 217.title: Aerospace Sheet Metal Fab
WELD 217.description: Sheet metal fabrication with an aerospace emphasis: projects from prints using flat pattern layout, bend sequencing, spot welding, pan and finger brakes, roll forming, and punching and notching.

WELD 225.title: Welding Skills Building
WELD 225.description: Extra lab practice before a state welding certification exam, or to sharpen skills. May be repeated two times for credit.

WELD 231.title: Welding Capstone
WELD 231.description: Building an aluminum boat hull with GTAW and GMAW, working to hull and structural welding codes (ABS Part 2, AWS D1.2, AWS D3.7) and evaluating welds against them.
WELD 231.prereq_text: MFG T 100; WELD 101, WELD 105, WELD 194, WELD 195

WELD 285.title: CNC Plasma/Waterjet Cutting
WELD 285.description: Automated manufacturing on three-axis CNC plasma and waterjet cutting equipment using several 2D CAD programs. May be repeated once for credit.

WELD 286.title: Aero CNC Plasma Cutting 2
WELD 286.description: Programming and operating a computerized plasma cutting system with AutoCAD for aerospace applications, including production parts, quality control, and industry tolerances.

WELD 295.title: Work Experience Internship
WELD 295.description: Supervised workplace practice of welding and fabrication skills. May be taken one additional time for credit.

ANTH& 206.title: Cultural Anthropology
ANTH& 206.description: Cross-cultural introduction to culture and society comparing family, kinship, economic, political and religious systems, with fieldwork and ethnographic writing methods.
ANTH& 206.prereq_text: ENGL& 101 with a grade of C or higher

BIOL 105.title: Disease In Modern Society
BIOL 105.description: Infectious disease, scientific inquiry and how biology applies to people and society; for non-science majors.
BIOL 105.prereq_text: Eligibility for ENGL& 101 AND eligibility for MATH 96

BIOL 130.title: Marine Biology Pacific NW
BIOL 130.description: Life processes and ecology of marine organisms, with field trips focused on intertidal communities of the Salish Sea. Covers the scientific method, oceanographic drivers, marine ecology, and identifying marine organisms.
BIOL 130.prereq_text: Eligibility for ENGL& 101 AND eligibility for MATH 96.
BIOL 130.placement: Eligibility for ENGL& 101 AND eligibility for MATH 96.

BIOL& 211.title: Majors Cellular
BIOL& 211.description: Principles of cellular biology and how they apply to organisms.
BIOL& 211.prereq_text: Eligibility for ENGL& 101, AND CHEM& 121, OR CHEM& 161 and CHEM& 162, each with a grade of C or higher.

BIOL& 231.title: Human Anatomy
BIOL& 231.description: Human body structure through models, skeletons, slides, digital media and dissection of animal specimens and a preserved cat; for allied health majors.
BIOL& 231.prereq_text: Completion of BIOL& 211, or BIOL& 221 AND BIOL& 222, each with a grade of C or higher; AND CHEM& 121 or CHEM& 161 AND 162, each with a grade of C or higher.

BIOL& 260.title: Microbiology
BIOL& 260.description: Survey of microbes and the biological processes they carry out, with a focus on bacteria.
BIOL& 260.prereq_text: BIOL& 211 and BIOL& 232; or BIOL& 222 and BIOL& 223; all with a grade of C or higher. All prerequisites must be taken within the last five years, or instructor permission.
BIOL& 260.placement: Prerequisites within the last five years, or instructor permission

BOT 113.title: Plants of the Pacific NW
BOT 113.description: Classification and identification of ferns, conifers and flowering plants, focused on Pacific Northwest flora. Includes plant naming, reproduction, ecology and human uses of plants.
BOT 113.prereq_text: Eligibility for ENGL& 101 AND eligibility for MATH 86.
BOT 113.placement: Eligibility for ENGL& 101 AND eligibility for MATH 86.

BT 219.title: Intro to MS Word
BT 219.description: Word processing with Microsoft Word: document creation, formatting, file management, merge, tables, pagination.

BT 242.title: Excel
BT 242.description: Intermediate and advanced Excel for polished multi-sheet workbooks using functions and templates.

BUS 130.title: Business Computations
BUS 130.description: Math applied to business data: percentages, banking, payroll, taxes, insurance, interest, mortgages and financial statements.

CHEM& 131.title: Intro to Organic/Biochem
CHEM& 131.description: Structure, naming and reactions of organic molecules, with an introduction to biochemistry.
CHEM& 131.prereq_text: CHEM& 121 or CHEM& 161 with a grade of C (2.0) or higher, BIOL& 211 with a grade of C (2.0) or higher AND eligibility for ENGL& 101; or instructor permission

CL 103.title: Word Processing
CL 103.description: Self-paced introductory Microsoft Word: document creation and formatting, tables, images and mail merge.

CL 104.title: Spreadsheets
CL 104.description: Self-paced introduction to Excel: creating and editing spreadsheets, formulas, charts and graphs.

CMST& 220.title: Public Speaking
CMST& 220.description: Speech writing and delivery: audience analysis, organization, source credibility, delivery and evaluation.

CMST& 240.title: Intercultural Communication
CMST& 240.description: How people from different cultural backgrounds communicate: verbal and nonverbal signals, values, identities, common barriers and skills to address them.

DRMA& 101.title: Introduction to the Theatre
DRMA& 101.description: Survey of major theatre forms, styles and movements and the roles of practitioners and audiences.

EMS 151.title: Emergency Med Tech Training
EMS 151.description: All phases of pre-hospital emergency care through lecture and hands-on practice. Completers are eligible for the NREMT exam and the Washington State EMT-B exam.
EMS 151.prereq_text: Eligibility for ENGL 097 or higher, AND Completion of MATH 076 or higher, an approved program application (including passing an EMS pre-test with a score of 80% or higher), AND Instructor Permission.
EMS 151.placement: Eligibility for ENGL 97 or higher; approved program application with EMS pre-test score of 80% or higher; instructor permission

EMS 155.title: Emergency Medical Technician - Snohomish County Emphasis
EMS 155.description: Field-based emergency care through lecture and hands-on practice, with added focus on Snohomish County pre-hospital skills and protocols. Completers qualify for the NREMT and Washington State EMT-B exams.
EMS 155.placement: Intended and designed for participants employed full-time with a Snohomish County fire department

ENGL 103.title: The Critical Paper
ENGL 103.description: Writing critical analysis of culture and the arts, including film, music, art and popular culture.

FILM 100.title: Introduction to Film
FILM 100.description: Form, style and cultural content of American and international film, and how design, cinematography, editing and sound shape style.

GEOL 104.title: Intro to Geol Science II
GEOL 104.description: Surface processes that shape Earth: rivers, glaciers, groundwater, oceans and deserts. Also covers geologic hazards, environmental geology and resource management, with hands-on labs and field work.
GEOL 104.prereq_text: Eligibility for ENGL& 101 AND eligibility for MATH 86.
GEOL 104.placement: Eligibility for ENGL& 101 AND eligibility for MATH 86.

GEOL& 103.title: Historical Geology
GEOL& 103.description: Geologic history of Earth with a focus on North America and the Pacific Northwest. Topics include plate tectonics, past environments, and the origin and evolution of life, with hands-on labs and field work.
GEOL& 103.prereq_text: Eligibility for ENGL& 101 AND eligibility for MATH 86.
GEOL& 103.placement: Eligibility for ENGL& 101 AND eligibility for MATH 86.

HCM 101.title: Intro to Healthcare Careers
HCM 101.description: Overview of clinical and administrative healthcare careers: job roles, duties, salary ranges, required education and job availability.

HCM 103.title: Intro to Admin Medical Office
HCM 103.description: Introduces medical office administrative programs, program tools, computer basics, student success, and healthcare careers on a coordinated care team. Equivalent to MC 103; credit cannot be earned for both.

HCM 107.title: Span Essentials for Healthcare
HCM 107.description: Prepares non-Spanish speakers to communicate at a basic level with Spanish-speaking patients: comfort and basic needs assessment, vocabulary, and cultural considerations in intake and triage.

HCM 120.title: Applied Medical Terminology
HCM 120.description: Medical word building (prefixes, suffixes, roots, abbreviations, eponyms) across body systems, with spelling, pronouncing and interpreting terms in a language lab. Equivalent to MC 120; credit cannot be earned in both.

HCM 128.title: Medical Coding for Non-Coders
HCM 128.description: Introduction to the common coding classification systems used in healthcare and the link between coding and reimbursement. Not intended for Medical Coding Certificate or Medical Billing and Coding ATA students.

HCM 137.title: Structure/Function Human Body
HCM 137.description: Non-lab, system-based study of the healthy human body, ending with a review that connects A&P to reading clinical documentation for code assignment. No prior biology or chemistry required. Equivalent to MC 137.

HCM 143.title: Pathophysiology & Pharmacology
HCM 143.description: Disease processes (causes, diagnosis, treatment) and how the body absorbs, distributes, metabolizes and excretes drugs. Equivalent to MC 143; credit cannot be earned in both.
HCM 143.prereq_text: HCM 120 or MC 120 or HCM 137 or MC 137, with a grade of C or higher

HCM 180.title: Principles of Med Insurance
HCM 180.description: The medical billing cycle, private and government insurance, HIPAA, claim forms, and a practice management system for registration, billing and payments.

HCM 181.title: Law/Ethics Healthcare Occup
HCM 181.description: Law and ethics in medical offices and patient-provider relationships, including informed consent, professional liability and allocation of scarce resources.

HCM 182.title: Medical Reception
HCM 182.description: Medical front office duties with HIPAA compliance: scheduling, communication with patients and staff, protecting patient information, and office safety.

HCM 187.title: Electronic Health Records
HCM 187.description: How personal health information is captured, used, stored and retrieved in paper, hybrid and electronic formats, with hands-on EHR experience.

HCM 206.title: Intro to Healthcare Risk Mgmt
HCM 206.description: Introduction to healthcare risk management: history, the risk manager's role, and compliance with federal and local agencies across healthcare settings.
HCM 206.prereq_text: Eligibility for ENGL& 101 or concurrent enrollment in ENGL 98.
HCM 206.placement: Eligibility for ENGL& 101 or concurrent enrollment in ENGL 98

HCM 207.title: Law/Healthcare/Patient Safety
HCM 207.description: Federal, state and local health and safety laws applied to risk management and patient safety: workplace hazards, accident prevention, emergency management.
HCM 207.prereq_text: Eligibility for ENGL& 101 or concurrent enrollment in ENGL 98
HCM 207.placement: Eligibility for ENGL& 101 or concurrent enrollment in ENGL 98

HCM 208.title: Healthcare Risk Mgmt/Liability
HCM 208.description: Malpractice and liability insurance, how malpractice cases are litigated and settled, accurate medical record documentation, and emerging liability risks.
HCM 208.prereq_text: Eligibility for ENGL& 101 or concurrent enrollment in ENGL 98.
HCM 208.placement: Eligibility for ENGL& 101 or concurrent enrollment in ENGL 98

HLTH 100.title: Medical Terminology
HLTH 100.description: Medical terms and how they relate to body anatomy and physiology. For students building medical language skills and those entering healthcare professions.

HLTH 102.title: Applied A & P
HLTH 102.description: How the body's structures relate to their functions and clinical applications in health and disease, including homeostasis. No prior biology or chemistry needed; familiarity with medical terminology is desired.

HLTH 109.title: First Aid & Basic Life Support
HLTH 109.description: American Heart Association Basic Life Support for adults, children and infants (CPR, AED, airway, rescue breathing) plus First Aid for life-threatening conditions.

HLTH 130.title: Disease & Pathology
HLTH 130.description: Survey of major diseases (infectious, neoplastic, congenital) first diagnosed in clinical settings: cause, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment, prognosis and prevention.
HLTH 130.prereq_text: HLTH 102, or BIOL& 231 and 232 or equivalent, each with a grade of C or higher

HLTH 135.title: Admin Skills: Office Management
HLTH 135.description: General medical office management: medical records, mail, appointment scheduling, the physician's calendar, office policies and procedures, and patient resources.
HLTH 135.prereq_text: Eligibility for ENGL& 101, and MATH 76 or TS 76 or higher, each with a grade of C or higher

HLTH 136.title: Admin Skills: Practice Finance
HLTH 136.description: Financial operations of a medical practice: record keeping, insurance billing, medical coding, accounting and banking tasks, and payroll.
HLTH 136.prereq_text: Eligibility for ENGL& 101, and MATH 76 or TS 76 or higher, each with a grade of C or higher

HLTH 150.title: Intercultural Comm in Hlthcare
HLTH 150.description: Interpersonal intercultural communication in healthcare: verbal and nonverbal communication, cultural competence, barriers to cross-cultural communication.
HLTH 150.prereq_text: Eligibility for ENGL& 101, and eligibility for MATH 86 or TS 86 or higher.
HLTH 150.placement: Eligibility for MATH 86 or TS 86 or higher

HLTH 160.title: Medical Interpreting-Spanish
HLTH 160.description: The role of a professional Spanish/English medical interpreter: standards, ethics, cultural advocacy, interpreting skills and medical vocabulary.
HLTH 160.prereq_text: HLTH 100 with a grade of C or higher, or concurrent enrollment

HLTH 205.title: Medical Law and Ethics
HLTH 205.description: Federal and state law in clinical practice (confidentiality, HIPAA, release of information, licensure, malpractice, risk management) and current bioethical issues.
HLTH 205.prereq_text: Completion of ENGL 98 or ENGL& 101, and MATH 76 or TS 76 or higher, each with a grade of C or higher

HLTH 210.title: Principles of Pharmacology
HLTH 210.description: Medication forms, drug classes, actions, uses and side effects, with patient safety and education. Emphasizes the 50 most commonly prescribed drugs; includes 20 hours of simulated clinical practice.
HLTH 210.prereq_text: Completion of ENGL 98 or ENGL& 101, and MATH 76 or TS 76 or higher, each with a grade of C or higher

HLTH 220.title: Phlebotomy Tech Training
HLTH 220.description: Prepares students with no prior phlebotomy experience for national certification exams: cardiovascular A&P, patient communication, ethics, blood collection, quality assurance and lab information (CLSI guidelines).

HLTH 221.title: Phlebotomy Tech Pract
HLTH 221.description: Phlebotomy practicum preparing for national certification exams. Includes a 120-hour unpaid clinical externship at area hospitals or clinics, arranged by the instructor.

HLTH 231.title: Clinical Skills - Surgical
HLTH 231.description: Hands-on surgical and clinical skills for medical assistants: sterile technique, safety, instrument sterilization, wound care, and assisting with minor office procedures.
HLTH 231.prereq_text: Completion of HLTH 135 or HLTH 136 with a grade of C or higher, and eligibility for ENGL& 101, and eligibility for MATH/TS 86 or higher. Immunizations required before instructor permission.

HLTH 232.title: Clinical Laboratory Skills
HLTH 232.description: Medical assistant laboratory duties in outpatient practice: lab safety, quality assurance, microbiology, transmission-based precautions, specimen collection and processing.
HLTH 232.prereq_text: HLTH 135 or HLTH 136 with a grade C or higher, and eligibility for ENGL& 101, and eligibility for MATH/TS 86 or higher. Instructor permission and immunizations required.

HLTH 241.title: Medication Administration
HLTH 241.description: Calculating, preparing and giving medications to patients of all ages, plus safety rules and legal duties in prescribing, dispensing and administering drugs.
HLTH 241.prereq_text: HLTH 241, HLTH 242 and HLTH 243 must be taken concurrently.

HLTH 242.title: Principles of Phlebotomy
HLTH 242.description: Hands-on blood-drawing procedures for students with no prior experience, plus documentation, common lab tests, quality control and lab safety.
HLTH 242.prereq_text: HLTH 241, HLTH 242 and HLTH 243 must be taken concurrently.

HLTH 243.title: Clinical Skills - Ambulatory
HLTH 243.description: Medical assisting skills supporting a licensed provider: patient communication, vital signs, exams and diagnostic procedures, preventive health coaching, maternal and pediatric care. Includes 20 hours of simulated clinical practice.
HLTH 243.prereq_text: HLTH 241, HLTH 242 and HLTH 243 must be taken concurrently.

HLTH 251.title: Clinical Practicum
HLTH 251.description: 160 supervised clinical hours in an outpatient ambulatory setting with weekly seminars on professional topics in medical assisting.
HLTH 251.prereq_text: Completion of all Medical Assisting courses with a C or higher, and instructor permission

HP 101.title: Coll Success for Health Prof
HP 101.description: Roles and professional traits in patient-care fields, plus academic and personal skills for college success. Satisfies the College Success requirement.

HUM& 101.title: Introduction to the Humanities
HUM& 101.description: Interdisciplinary introduction to the humanities as a way to explore meaning, value and human experience, with emphasis on reading, critical thinking and writing.

MATH 138.title: Applied College Algebra
MATH 138.description: College algebra with applications: functions, equations and systems, matrices, linear programming and the mathematics of finance. For business, social science and some life science students, not math, science or engineering majors.
MATH 138.prereq_text: MATH 96 or equivalent with a grade of C or higher

MATH 76.title: Mathematical Literacy
MATH 76.description: Review of foundational math with real-world applications: factorization, rational numbers, algebraic expressions, percentages, graphs and linear relationships.

MC 103.title: Intro to Admin Med Office
MC 103.description: Introduces medical office administrative programs, program tools, computer basics, student success resources and medical care team roles. Equivalent to HCM 103; credit cannot be earned for both.

MC 118.title: Health Info/Delivery Systems
MC 118.description: Health data standards and structure, healthcare delivery systems and health IT: record data, security, documentation, facility operations and regulation.
MC 118.prereq_text: MC 103 or HCM 103 with a grade of C, or higher or concurrent enrollment

MC 120.title: Applied Medical Terminology
MC 120.description: Medical terminology for healthcare management: prefixes, suffixes, roots, abbreviations and eponyms across body systems, practiced in a language lab. Equivalent to HCM 120.

MC 137.title: Structure/Function Human Body
MC 137.description: Non-lab, system-based study of the healthy human body tied to reading clinical documentation for code assignment. No prior biology or chemistry required. Equivalent to HCM 137.

MC 143.title: Pathophysiology & Pharmacology
MC 143.description: Disease processes (causes, diagnosis, treatment) and how the body handles medications, for professional healthcare communication. Equivalent to HCM 143; credit cannot be earned in both.
MC 143.prereq_text: MC 120 or HCM 120 or MC 137 or HCM 137, with a grade of C or higher

MC 147.title: Intro to Diagnosis Coding
MC 147.description: Diagnostic coding principles and the ICD system, plus taxonomies, nomenclatures, clinical vocabularies and official coding guidelines.
MC 147.prereq_text: MC 143 or HCM 143 with a grade of C or higher, or concurrent enrollment

MC 151.title: Intro to Procedure Coding
MC 151.description: Procedure coding principles: reviewing medical records, applying guidelines, assigning procedural codes across settings, and coding references.
MC 151.prereq_text: MC 137 or HCM 137 with a grade of C of higher

MC 218.title: Hlthcare Reimbur/Legal Compli
MC 218.description: How coded data is used in reimbursement: payment methods, prospective payment systems, health plans, chargemaster maintenance, compliant billing and legal issues for coders.
MC 218.prereq_text: MC 118 with a grade of C or higher

MC 247.title: Advanced Diagnosis Coding
MC 247.description: Advanced diagnostic coding: severity of illness systems, compliance, SNOMED, crosswalks and maps, complex cases and DRG-based payment.
MC 247.prereq_text: MC 147 with a grade of C or higher

MC 251.title: Advanced Procedure Coding
MC 251.description: Advanced procedure coding: prospective payment applications, professional fee billing (E/M, surgical services), and complex Level I and II code assignment.
MC 251.prereq_text: MC 151 with a grade of C or higher

MC 280.title: Prof Practice Experience
MC 280.description: Coding practice from real patient charts in a healthcare setting across inpatient, outpatient, physician, ER and long-term care cases, with encoder software.
MC 280.prereq_text: Completion of all required courses in Medical Coding (MC/HCM 103, MC 118, MC/HCM 120, MC/HCM 137, MC/HCM 143, MC 147, MC 151, MC 218, MC 247, MC 251), with a C or higher

MUSC 110.title: World Music
MUSC 110.description: Survey of music from non-Western regions: history, performance practice, aural identification and musical exchange.

MUSC 115.title: Popular Music In America
MUSC 115.description: Historical, social and stylistic survey of 20th-century American popular music.

MUSC 116.title: Survey of Jazz
MUSC 116.description: Historical, social and stylistic development of jazz from its African roots to contemporary jazz.

MUSC& 105.title: Music Appreciation
MUSC& 105.description: Structure, form and historical development of western music for the listener.

NURS 100.title: Nursing Assistant
NURS 100.description: Basic technical skills, client rights, communication, safety and emergency procedures, personal care, restorative services, infection control, HIV information, and the rules that govern nursing assistant practice.
NURS 100.prereq_text: Pre/Corequisites: HLTH 109 (or concurrent enrollment) or equivalent, with a grade of C (2.0) or higher.

NURS 110.title: Nursing Therapeutics I
NURS 110.description: Caring as a framework for nursing practice: the client, health environment, nursing process, communication, teaching and learning, and ethics. Lab covers health promotion, assessment, documentation and basic skills.
NURS 110.prereq_text: Prerequisite: Acceptance into the Nursing program. Corequisites: NURS 114 / PHIL 114

NURS 120.title: Nursing Therapeutics II
NURS 120.description: Integrated view of mind and body responses to chronic health conditions; cognitive, interpersonal and technical skills for adult clients. Includes lab.
NURS 120.prereq_text: Prerequisites: Completion of NURS 110. Corequisites: NURS 125 / PSYC 125 and NURS 126 /NUTR 126

NURS 130.title: Nursing Therapeutics III
NURS 130.description: Complex body system alterations and related nursing therapies, with emphasis on critical thinking and nursing judgment. Includes lab.
NURS 130.prereq_text: Prerequisites: Completion of NURS 120. Corequisites: NURS 136 / NUTR 136

NURS 210.title: Nursing Therapeutics IV
NURS 210.description: Integrated view of normal growth and development from infancy to adolescence and the expanding family, using the nursing process. Includes lab.
NURS 210.prereq_text: Prerequisites: Completion of NURS 130. Corequisites: NURS 214 / PHIL 214 and NURS 216 / NUTR 216

NURS 220.title: Nursing Therapeutics V
NURS 220.description: Physical and mental health conditions affecting multiple body systems and related nursing therapies; complex client care skills in collaboration with other professionals. Includes lab.
NURS 220.prereq_text: Prerequisites: Completion of NURS 210. Corequisites: NURS 225 / PSYC 225 and NURS 226 / NUTR 226

NURS 230.title: Nurs/Thera VI-Transition
NURS 230.description: Professional nursing practice: values, ethics, accountability, power and politics, collective bargaining and healthcare business, with clinical experiences for role transition.
NURS 230.prereq_text: Prerequisites: Completion of NURS 220. Corequisites: NURS 234 / PHIL 234 and NURS 235 / PSYC 235

NUTR 126.title: Nutrition in Healthcare I
NUTR 126.description: Adult nutrition, nutritional assessment, chronic disease such as diabetes, enteral and parenteral feeding, applied in long-term care clinicals.
NUTR 126.prereq_text: Prerequisite: Completion of NURS 110 with a C or higher. Corequisites: NURS 120 and NURS 125/PSYC 125

NUTR 136.title: Nutrition in Healthcare II
NUTR 136.description: Adult nutrition, specialty diets for acute and chronic conditions, and nutritional assessment with hospitalized patients.
NUTR 136.prereq_text: Prerequisite: Completion of NURS 120 with a C or higher. Corequisites: NURS 130

NUTR 216.title: Nutrition in Healthcare III
NUTR 216.description: Infant, maternal and pediatric nutrition: growth assessment, metabolic conditions and specialty diets, applied in clinicals.
NUTR 216.prereq_text: Prerequisite: Completion of NURS 130 with a C or higher. Corequisites: NURS 210 and NURS 214/PHIL 214

NUTR 226.title: Nutrition in Healthcare IV
NUTR 226.description: Adult nutrition and its effect on wound healing, chronic and acute disease, and parenteral/TPN care in acute care settings.
NUTR 226.prereq_text: Completion of NURS 210 with a C or higher. Corequisites: NURS 220 and NURS 225/PSYC 225

PHIL 110.title: Social Ethics
PHIL 110.description: Examines contemporary controversial social issues through independent thinking and dialogue; topics vary by year.

PHIL 114.title: Ethics & Policy Healthcare I
PHIL 114.description: Values, ethics, and legal decision-making frameworks and policies in the healthcare professions, taught with NURS 110.
PHIL 114.prereq_text: Concurrent enrolled in NURS 110; AND successful admission into EvCC Nursing Program.

PHIL 214.title: Ethics/Policy Healthcare II
PHIL 214.description: Applies values, ethics and legal decision-making frameworks and policies in the healthcare professions, taught with NURS 210.
PHIL 214.prereq_text: Concurrent enrollment in NURS 210, NURS 216/NUTR 216; AND completion of NURS 130.

PHIL 215.title: Ethics
PHIL 215.description: Survey of major historical and modern questions in moral philosophy and why moral judgments differ.

PHIL 234.title: Ethics/Policy Healthcare III
PHIL 234.description: Ethical, legal and policy frameworks in the healthcare professions, taught with NURS 230.
PHIL 234.prereq_text: Concurrent enrollment in NURS 230, NURS 235/PSYC 235; AND completion of NURS 220.

PHIL 267.title: Philosophy of Religion
PHIL 267.description: Philosophical study of religious thought centered on Christian theology and philosophy, also including Judaism, Islam, Buddhism and Hinduism.

PHIL& 101.title: Introduction to Philosophy
PHIL& 101.description: Survey of major questions in philosophical thought: reality, knowledge, personal identity and the mind.

PHIL& 115.title: Critical Thinking
PHIL& 115.description: Analyzing, evaluating and constructing thought in clear logical fashion, with application to various fields.

PHYS& 115.title: General Physics II
PHYS& 115.description: Second course of the algebra-based General Physics sequence (PHYS& 114-116): periodic motion, mechanical waves and thermodynamics.
PHYS& 115.prereq_text: PHYS& 114 AND MATH 138 or MATH& 142 or MATH& 144 or equivalent, each with a grade of C or higher

PHYS& 116.title: General Physics III
PHYS& 116.description: Third course in the one-year algebra-based General Physics sequence (PHYS& 114-116). Covers electricity, magnetism and light.
PHYS& 116.prereq_text: PHYS& 114 AND MATH& 142 or MATH& 144 or equivalent, each with a grade C or higher

PSYC 125.title: Psychosocial Issues I
PSYC 125.description: Social, psychological, environmental, spiritual and cultural factors in health and illness across the lifespan, taught with NURS 120.
PSYC 125.prereq_text: Concurrent enrollment in NURS 120, NURS 126/NUTR 126; AND completion of NURS 110.

PSYC 215.title: Psychosocial Issues II
PSYC 215.description: Social, mental, environmental, spiritual and cultural influences on wellness and illness across the lifespan, taught with NURS 210.
PSYC 215.prereq_text: NURS 130, and concurrent enrollment in NURS 210

PSYC 225.title: Psychosocial Issues III
PSYC 225.description: Social, psychological, environmental, spiritual and cultural factors in health and illness, taught with NURS 220.
PSYC 225.prereq_text: Concurrent enrollment in NURS 220, NURS 226/NUTR 226; AND completion of NURS 210.

PSYC 235.title: Psychosocial Issues IV
PSYC 235.description: Social, mental, environmental, faith-related and cultural influences on health and illness, taught with NURS 230.
PSYC 235.prereq_text: Concurrent enrollment in NURS 230. NURS 234/NUTR 234; AND completion of NURS 220.

PSYC& 100.title: General Psychology
PSYC& 100.description: Psychology as a science, using a biopsychosocial approach to behavior and mental processes: the brain, learning, research methods and disorders.

PSYC& 200.title: Lifespan Psychology
PSYC& 200.description: Physical, emotional, social and cognitive changes from conception to death.
PSYC& 200.prereq_text: PSYC& 100 with a grade of C or higher, AND eligibility for ENGL& 101

SOC& 101.title: Introduction to Sociology
SOC& 101.description: General survey of society's cultural and social systems and how they shape individual lives.

TS 76.title: Mathematical Literacy
TS 76.description: Transitional Studies review of basic math with real-world applications: fractions, ratios, percentages, algebraic expressions, graphs and linear relationships.
TS 76.prereq_text: Eligibility for HSC 76 or TS 76 or MATH 76. Students must have completed the TS orientation & assessment or taken a TS class within the last 6 months.
TS 76.placement: TS orientation and assessment, or a TS class in the last 6 months
