advisor_notes.text: All four science AS-T degrees require a 2.0 (C) or higher in prerequisites, and the catalog says science sequences should not be split between colleges.
Bio, Chem and Geology are AS-T Track 1. Physics and Astronomy is AS-T Track 2. None of the four is labeled MRP in the 2026-2027 catalog.
CHEM& 261-263 (Organic) run only Fall, Winter, Spring in sequence. Bio and Chem students must start organic in Fall.

EvCC Nursing is selective. NURS 110 requires acceptance into the Nursing program, and a required non-credit class (permission required) must be finished before you submit the Nursing Program application. The 2026-27 catalog does not list admission points, GPA cutoffs, deadlines, immunization or background check rules for nursing, so check the EvCC Nursing program office for the current application packet.

For the Nursing DTA, the five Natural Science courses (BIOL& 211, 231, 232, 260 and CHEM& 121) need an overall 3.0 GPA, with no course below 2.0. Each NURS core course needs 2.7 or higher; the NUTR, PHIL and PSYC core pieces need 2.0.

The biology chain for nursing takes at least four quarters after CHEM& 121: BIOL& 211, then BIOL& 231, then BIOL& 232, then BIOL& 260. BIOL& 232 and BIOL& 260 require their prerequisites within the last five years (or instructor permission), so students should not start the chain too early.

ANTH& 206 counts as a Communication Skills course in the Nursing DTA only if taken at EvCC. In the Pre-Nursing DTA, students choose ANTH& 206 or SOC& 101 in Social Sciences, so ANTH& 206 is the choice that also fits the Nursing DTA.

The Pre-Nursing DTA (90 units) prepares students to apply to nursing programs, including EvCC's. It shares most science and general education courses with the Nursing DTA but adds ENGL& 102, CMST& 220, CHEM& 131 and NUTR& 101, which many BSN programs ask for. RN licensure requires finishing a nursing program and passing the NCLEX.

The Allied Health DTA lists specialization courses. Dental Hygiene (EWU, Lake Washington Tech, Bellingham Tech, Shoreline, Seattle Central): BIOL& 260, NUTR& 101, CHEM& 131. Diagnostic Medical Sonography (Seattle U, Tacoma CC): MATH& 141 and 142, PHYS& 114 and 115, CHEM& 161, BIOL& 231 and 232. Bellevue College sonography: PHYS 100 (at Bellevue) or MATH& 141 and 142, plus PHYS& 114 at EvCC. The page also names echocardiography, radiation technology and respiratory therapy but lists no courses for them. Confirm with each school.

Medical Assistant students should start immunizations in their first quarter. They take 8-9 months, HLTH 231 and 232 need them before instructor permission, and all vaccines are required before Phase Four (HLTH 241, 242, 243, 251).

The Medical Assistant Certificate (73-74 units) is completed inside the ATA (add 14-15 elective units to reach 90) and the AAS-T (add 23 units of English, math, CS or logic, science and a humanities elective). The AAS-T is built for transfer to CWU's BAS in Information Technology and Administrative Management or City University of Seattle's BS in Health Administration.

Washington medical assistants must hold the state MA-C credential. EvCC's accredited program plus a passing score on one of five national exams meets the requirement (WA DOH lists AAMA CMA, AMT RMA, NHA CCMA, NCCT NCMA and AMCA CMAC).

MC and HCM versions of the same course (103, 120, 137, 143) are interchangeable in the billing and coding programs, but credit cannot be earned in both. HCM 128 (in the Billing Specialist Certificate) is not meant for Medical Coding Certificate or ATA students.

EvCC's Medical Coding program is AHIMA-approved, so Medical Coding Certificate and Medical Billing and Coding ATA graduates can sit for the AHIMA Certified Coding Associate (CCA) exam. The Billing Specialist Certificate can stack into the ATA.

Phlebotomy students need a national background check, a compliant Complio immunization account, ENGL& 101 eligibility and an AHA BLS card before starting. Working as a phlebotomist in Washington requires the DOH Medical Assistant-Phlebotomist (MA-P) credential; NHA CPT and NCCT certifications are optional.

EMT: EMS 151 requires an approved application and an EMS pre-test score of 80% or higher. After passing the NREMT, students must get EMT work within 12 months to become Washington EMT certified, or retake the whole course.

Washington DSHS accepts CCHI and NBCMI written and oral tests for Spanish medical interpreter certification. The EvCC catalog does not say whether HLTH 160 alone meets those boards' training-hour requirements.

EvCC calculus physics order (PHYS& 241 mechanics, 242 heat and waves, 243 E&M) does not match UW's (PHYS 121 mechanics, 122 E&M, 123 waves and heat). UW's 2024 Everett planning sheet shows PHYS& 242/232 as PHYS 2XX. Check MyPlan before a student applies to UW Physics or Astronomy.
EvCC algebra physics also differs: UW maps PHYS& 115 (waves, thermo) to PHYS 116 and PHYS& 116 (E&M) to PHYS 115.

Organic chemistry: UW and UW Bothell credit CHEM& 261-263 as a full series. WWU warns that transfer organic chemistry does not count toward upper-division major credits; EWU's organic sequence is upper-division. Have WWU and EWU students ask the department before finishing CHEM& 263.
EvCC has no GEOL& 101. Its physical geology course is GEOL 102 (with GEOL 104 and GEOL& 103 Historical Geology). University geology equivalents for these were not confirmed for any school.

Capacity-constrained or application majors in this slice: UW Biochemistry, UW Physics, UW Astronomy, WWU Chemistry and Biochemistry. Open or declare-on-arrival: UW Chemistry (minimums), UW ESS, WSU Chemistry, Physics and Astronomy, and Earth Sciences, WWU Physics, CWU and EWU majors.

EvCC teaches A&P as BIOL& 231 Human Anatomy and BIOL& 232 Human Physiology, not BIOL& 241/242. Universities that list BIOL& 241/242 (UW Tacoma) or 'A&P I and II' accept the pair; UW gives full credit only when both are taken.
Pre-Nursing DTA students aiming at UW Seattle or Seattle U need one extra college-level math course (MATH& 141 or higher; UW also accepts a logic course). Statistics alone does not cover it.
In the Pre-Nursing DTA, pick SOC& 101 over ANTH& 206 if WSU or Walla Walla is a target. WSU lists Intro to Sociology as a BSN prerequisite.
UW Seattle requires 100 hours of hands-on health care experience in the 12 months before applying. WSU counts up to 500 hours but does not require them. SPU, Seattle U and PLU do not require hours.
Only WSU requires the TEAS (70 or higher) among the pre-licensure BSN programs covered. UW, SPU and Seattle U say TEAS is not required.

EvCC ADN graduates: UW Bothell's Nurse Scholars Program lists EvCC as a partner (simpler application, fee waived, start within 15 months of the ADN). The Winter cohort meets at the Everett University Center.
The EvCC Associate in Nursing DTA does not include NUTR& 101 or SOC& 101. WSU's RN to BSN lists Human Nutrition and Intro to Sociology as prerequisites, so check with WSU before a student applies.

EvCC's Allied Health DTA (CHEM& 121, BIOL& 211, 231, 232, HLTH 100, PSYC& 100) lines up best with dental hygiene, respiratory care and the UW Public Health-Global Health BA path. Students aiming for sonography also need MATH& 141/142, PHYS& 114/115 and CHEM& 161; students aiming for a public health BS or WSU nutrition need the majors chemistry and biology sequences.

Many dental hygiene and respiratory care programs list A&P as BIOL& 241/242. EvCC's A&P is BIOL& 231 (Anatomy) and BIOL& 232 (Physiology); EvCC's BIOL& 241/242 are transfer-in placeholders only. Shoreline's equivalence guide confirms 231 = 241 and 232 = 242. For other schools, have students confirm before applying.
Science time limits differ: EWU and LWTech dental hygiene, and Seattle U sonography, want science within 5 years; Shoreline allows 7 years. Seattle Central respiratory care limits only A&P (5 years).

For Medical Assistant graduates, Edmonds IHCM names Medical Assisting as an accepted field and Seattle Central HSM accepts allied health AAS-T degrees by name (with 1 year of work). EvCC's own MA AAS-T page names CWU ITAM and CityU BSHA.

For Medical Billing and Coding graduates, Tacoma CC's HIM BAS is the main health information management option in western Washington (RHIA eligible; CPC/CCS help in selection). Bellevue's Healthcare Informatics BAS is online with 24 first-come seats.
